sources.facts: Columbia’s record identifies the Istanbul Edirnekapı mosque and gives dome diameter 20 m and dome height 37 m.

The ministry describes Sinan’s rectangular hall with four main piers, side galleries behind three arches, highly windowed tympana, one slender late minaret on its original base, and the madrasa cells around the court. Written descriptions only.

Köse and Hamzaoğlu draw on Ottoman archive records to explain the successive repairs and post-earthquake reconstruction. The 1894 earthquake damaged the portico and minaret. The section and historical photo document the original form without adoption of the damage.
Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University identifies Gurlitt’s 1912 printed work as public domain. The Getty’s second volume contains these exact two plates.
